Issued at 344 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

===== Continued Messy Showers and Gradual Clearing West =====

Still dealing with the remnants of Isaias now as clusters or bands 
of showers will drift north while pivoting around the center of 
Isaias through the morning. There have been some decent soakers of 
heavier showers in these clusters, with Allen County having reported 
an additional 0.4" of rain since midnight. MUCAPE values have crept 
up to 500 J/kg in our SE CWA, and with enough lift, some showers 
could very briefly produce a lightning strike or two, though winds 
will remain light overnight and no severe weather is expected with 
anything that falls. Temperatures have all but reached their minimum 
with widespread temps in and around 60 this morning and will be 
sluggish to warm through the day on Sunday. Low hanging stratus and 
NE to eventually NW flow is the primary culprit in keeping highs 
cooler in the low 70s and upper 60s tomorrow. 

Similar to now, clusters of showers will continue to pivot around 
the center of Isaias Sunday morning and will begin to move east 
towards I-75 and beyond by the afternoon hours. Should they grow 
tall enough, a rumble of thunder is possible but otherwise, hit or 
miss showers are expected. Additional rainfall today will vary 
greatly across the CWA. With the scattered nature and positioning of 
the clusters of showers, SW Indiana counties like Dubois and Perry 
may largely miss out on additional rainfall remaining under 0.1" of 
rain. Closer to central KY and in the Bluegrass region, as these 
clusters pivot, some heavier showers could drop an additional 1-3" 
of rain in isolated areas (according to HREF 24 hr LPMM data). 
However, the 25th-75th percentile range favors 0.25-0.5" across most 
of the CWA, with closer to 0.5-1" centered in area spanning from E-
town to Shelby County.

As rain moves eastward, gradual raising of low level stratus and at 
least partial clearing in the western CWA will occur by mid 
afternoon somewhere between 1-5 PM EDT. Should breaks in the clouds 
occur earlier, some western towns like Huntingburg, IN could reach 
the mid to upper 70s but this will depend on the speed of Isaias 
finally leaving us. Regardless, the eastern CWA will stay socked 
into moisture throughout the day it seems and may hang on to showers 
and patchy drizzle until late Sunday night. With drying and clearing 
skies overnight Sunday into Monday morning, patchy fog will develop 
especially in the western CWA up until near the I-65 corridor. 
Communities east of there that might hang on to clouds a little 
longer may avoid fog formation or at least become even more patchy 
Monday morning.


===== Wave of Warmth Followed with Daily Rain Chances =====

Once Isaias finally gets kicked out of here by the mid level jet 
over the northern US, ridging will build back in its place. This 
will amplify a return to warm, SW flow and at least an initial dry 
spell from Monday through Tuesday. Sunny to mostly sunny skies are 
expected both days with highs in the low to mid 80s Monday to mid to 
upper 80s on Tuesday. Definitely a pattern flip from what we're 
experiencing now. By Wednesday however, the ridge to our south will 
itself dive a little further south allowing for a stalled out 
boundary along a deep digging trough over the central US to creep 
its way into the Ohio Valley. Tuesday will remain dry as shortwaves 
are expected to drift too far north to bring rain into our area. 
However, as the trough continues to slowly trudge eastward, multiple 
impulses or at least a steady plum of Pacific/Gulf moisture will 
keep rain and storm chances around (provided a strong enough trigger 
exists) will bring decent PoPs back into the CWA. Depending on how 
quickly this slow moving boundary can dive south through the CWA, 
will dictate how warm we will be by the middle to latter part of the 
week. Highs trend cooler with time and may return to the low 70s by 
Friday.
